# PresenterView

**Class:** `UltraCanvasPresenterView` · **Group:** [Text, images and media](../Groups/Text-images-and-media.md) · **Header:** [`UltraCanvas/include/UltraCanvasSlideShowPlayer.h`](../../../UltraCanvas/include/UltraCanvasSlideShowPlayer.h) · `#include "UltraCanvasSlideShowPlayer.h"`

**Inherits:** [`UltraCanvasContainer`](UltraCanvasContainer.md) → [`UltraCanvasUIElement`](UltraCanvasUIElement.md) → `Element`

## What it is for

The **presenter's screen** beside a show: the slide shown and the next, the speaker notes, the time with pause and reset, "Slide N of M", buttons that drive the player; `StartSlideShow` opens both on two monitors

## Overview

The presenter's screen: the slide shown, large; the next slide, small; the slide's speaker notes (scrollable); the time since the show began, with Pause / Resume and Reset; Previous slide and Next slide buttons; and "Slide N of M". It follows a player (SetPlayer) and drives it: its buttons and the keys typed into it go to the player, so the presenter can work the show from either screen.

## Creating it

Factory functions (the usual way - every element is held in a `std::shared_ptr`):

```cpp
std::shared_ptr<UltraCanvasPresenterView> CreatePresenterView(const std::string& id, int x, int y, int w, int h);
```

Constructors:

```cpp
UltraCanvasPresenterView(const std::string& id, int x, int y, int w, int h);
```

The first string argument is always the element's **identifier**, never its text (see [Core concepts](../Core-Concepts.md#identifiers)).

### struct `SlideShowWindows`

The windows of a show StartSlideShow opened. Keep it until onEnd: the windows close when the show ends (Escape, on from the end screen, or a window closed), and then onEnd runs.
